_comment: Sites used by the analog pipeline. role: analog = Earth candidate, target = Moon/Mars site, control = Earth site that should score LOW against every target. Earth sites list `types` (see config/site_types.json); a target has one `type`. window_km is the side of the square study area; diameter_km normalises crater profiles. Coordinates verified 2026-11-14 unless `verify` says otherwise.

sites.name: Haughton Crater
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: NASA Haughton-Mars Project site since 1997: polar desert, ~39 Myr old impact crater, ground ice.

sites.name: Mistastin Lake Crater
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Impact into anorthosite, the dominant rock of the lunar highlands. Crater floor is mostly a lake.

sites.name: Pingualuit Crater
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Young (~1.4 Myr), almost perfectly round simple crater holding a deep, clear lake.

sites.name: HMP base-camp plateau
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Plateau on the NW rim of Haughton where the Haughton-Mars Project research station has operated since 2000.

sites.name: Expedition Fiord uplands
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Around the McGill Arctic Research Station: high-Arctic uplands, low sun for months, nearby perennial cold springs.

sites.name: Tuktoyaktuk pingos
sites.region: Pingo Canadian Landmark, Northwest Territories, Canada
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Ice-cored hills (pingos) on ice-rich coastal plains, including Ibyuk, Canada's tallest pingo.

sites.name: Athabasca Sand Dunes
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Among the most northerly active dune fields on Earth. Waiting for a high-resolution Mars dune target.

sites.name: Spotted Lake (Kliluk)
sites.verify: coordinates approximate, not confirmed by search
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Magnesium-sulfate lake, a Mars sulfate analog. Needs mineral layers (CRISM) and a Mars evaporite target.

sites.name: Prairie control
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Flat farmland. Should score low against every target.

sites.name: Coast Mountains control
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Steep glaciated mountains: rugged, but no crater structure and little flat ground.

sites.name: Canadian Shield control
sites.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / AWS Open Data)
sites.blurb: Glacially scoured lakes and low hills, similar latitude and rock age to Mistastin.

sites.name: Jezero Crater
sites.source: Mars HRSC-MOLA Blended DEM v2, 200 m (USGS Astrogeology)
sites.blurb: Perseverance rover landing site: ancient lake with a river delta.
earth_limits: Mars gravity is 0.38 g: crater walls, slopes and ejecta behave differently.
Atmosphere is ~0.6% of Earth's pressure, mostly CO2: no liquid water today.
No magnetic field: surface radiation far above Earth levels.
Mean surface temperature about -60 C.

sites.name: Arcadia Planitia
sites.source: Mars HRSC-MOLA Blended DEM v2, 200 m (USGS Astrogeology)
sites.blurb: Smooth, low plains with shallow buried water ice (SHARAD radar, SWIM project pilot area): a proposed human landing region.
earth_limits: Mars gravity is 0.38 g and the air is ~0.6% of Earth's pressure: ice sublimates instead of melting.
Ice here is buried under dry regolith; Earth permafrost has an active layer that thaws every summer.
No magnetic field: surface radiation far above Earth levels.
200 m elevation data cannot see metre-scale polygons; HiRISE DEMs would be needed.

sites.name: Shackleton Crater
sites.source: LRO NAC 4 m stereo DEM (USGS, 'Moon LRO South Pole DEM') resampled to 20 m, LOLA LDEM_80S_80M fills the edges
sites.blurb: Rim lies almost on the south pole; permanently shadowed floor near Artemis candidate regions.
earth_limits: Moon gravity is 0.165 g: much deeper, steeper fresh craters for the same size.
Hard vacuum and no weathering: craters stay sharp for billions of years.
Permanently shadowed floors reach ~40 K (-233 C), colder than anywhere on Earth.
No atmosphere or magnetic field to block radiation and micrometeorites.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.region: Artemis III candidate region, lunar south pole
sites.source: LRO LOLA polar DEM LDEM_80S_80M (NASA PDS Geosciences)
sites.blurb: ~5 km high massif facing Earth: long sunlight on its heights and direct line of sight for communications.
earth_limits: At the lunar pole the Sun never rises more than ~1.5 deg: Earth sites only see this low sun part of the year.
Moon gravity is 0.165 g and there is no atmosphere: no wind, no erosion, regolith stays loose.
Day/night temperature swings of ~250 K in sunlit areas.
No atmosphere or magnetic field to block radiation and micrometeorites.

sites.name: Mons Mouton Plateau
sites.region: Artemis III candidate region, lunar south pole
sites.source: LRO LOLA polar DEM LDEM_80S_80M (NASA PDS Geosciences)
sites.blurb: The widest, flattest Artemis region. Centred on the IM-2 lander's 2025 touchdown point.
earth_limits: At the lunar pole the Sun never rises more than ~1.5 deg: Earth sites only see this low sun part of the year.
Moon gravity is 0.165 g and there is no atmosphere: no wind, no erosion, regolith stays loose.
Day/night temperature swings of ~250 K in sunlit areas.
No atmosphere or magnetic field to block radiation and micrometeorites.
